rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## Talking about money without flinching Money is the theme adults discuss in whispers and good essays discuss in plain sentences. Every candidate already runs a micro-economy — pocket money, top-ups, exam fees — and Nepal's macro-story (remittances, tourism, the tap of QR payments) is in the news you already scroll.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ## The debates, held honestly **"Money can't buy happiness"** is the theme's classic dialectic, and it deserves better than a slogan. Concede the ceiling: beyond needs and modest security, more money adds little to a Tuesday. Rebut the romance: poverty purchases misery with terrible reliability — money buys medicine, schooling, time and options, which is what happiness is made *of*.…  ·  ## Writing the theme — the report and the essay **The trend report** is this unit's genre: a chart or table given, language demanded. Trends have verbs — *rose, climbed, soared*; *fell, dropped, plunged*; *remained steady, fluctuated* — and the report wants the overall direction first, then the extremes, then one inference. Never narrate every number; select like a journalist.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## How the exam asks it The **essay** ("Money can't buy happiness", "Foreign employment: boon or bane") wants the dialectic shape, one Nepal anchor, one apt proverb — and no invented decimals. rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Can money buy happiness? (2 marks) — money secures basics and reduces stress, but relationships and purpose matter more; conclude clearly.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The words that carry the theme The everyday layer first, because the exam sets it there: **income, expenditure, budget, savings, debt, interest, loan, instalment, tax, subsidy, remittance, inflation, recession**. The digital layer: **mobile banking, digital wallet, QR payment, e-commerce, OTP fraud, phishing**.…  ·  ## Reading the theme like a writer — the devices of money talk Money language is a museum of **euphemism**, and noticing it is analysis: a company "right-sizes" (fires), a price "adjusts" (rises), a loan is a "financial product" (a debt), a gambler "invests" (loses).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Economic passages use cause-effect chains (inflation → prices → demand) — map the chain before answering comprehension questions.  ·  Trick 2: 'Money and happiness' essays: state what money CAN buy (security) and cannot (meaning), then conclude — the two-column frame wins.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Why do people save money? (1 mark) — security against emergencies and future goals.
